items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: single-detached housing sits on fee-simple lots on the residential streets east and north of downtown under RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%. Those are the zone's subdivision minimums, not a claim that every existing lot meets them. Town Centre parcels carry Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same bylaw.

Bare-land strata: present only as a scattered form, no named plan: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure: the buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the bylaws, and diligence runs through the Form B.

These are policy designations over largely built parcels — any assembly is a private negotiation over built lots, not a listed vacant-land offering. The City names a downtown location "Brickwater" at 11897 227 Street, but official City pages do not state its building type or developer.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around East Central

items.t: Main roads: Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) along the south side; Dewdney Trunk Road east–west through downtown and the residential area to the east; 224 Street and 226 Street north–south through the downtown core; the Haney Bypass links Lougheed Highway to Port Haney at the southwest corner.

Transit anchors: Haney Place Exchange is in this sub-area (routes include the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791); the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs from Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place; Port Haney Station, 22300 River Road, at the southwest corner, runs weekday West Coast Express trains between Waterfront and Mission City.

Schools physically inside the sub-area (Ministry-listed names only): Golden Ears Elementary (K–7), 23124 118 Avenue; Harry Hooge Elementary (K–7), 12280 230 Street; Thomas Haney Secondary (7–12), 23000 116 Avenue; ci:tməxw Environmental Community (K–8), 23125 116 Avenue; District 42 Alternative Secondary (9–12), 23125 116 Avenue. SD42 has no middle tier: elementary is K–7 and secondary is 8–12, with Thomas Haney listed at 7–12 on the provincial list.

Civic anchors: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place; Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road (City Hall, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, The ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall around it; Cenotaph, Bandstand, Haney Farmers Market); Maple Ridge Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library), 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, the only FVRL branch in Maple Ridge; Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre inside Haney Place Mall, 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, west of this sub-area, with 24/7 emergency care.

items.t: Density policy is the land story here, not vacant lots. Town Centre parcels: Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 govern the downtown core parcels.

Market thinness, labelled correctly: SnapStats has no land category (Detached vs "Condos & Townhomes" combined; Maple Ridge community detached median $1,131,000 and attached median $525,000 that month) — no detached or attached figure is presented as a land figure. blocks.text: Bare-land strata

items.t: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure — the buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata bylaws, and diligence runs through the Form B, exactly as with any strata; what differs is that the lot itself is bare land / a detached-house lot rather than a unit in a shared building envelope.
Do not quote a plan number, a lot count or a fee for a bare-land strata lot here until the title and Form B are pulled.

blocks.text: Land assemblies / development sites

items.t: Town Centre Core / River Bend (plan designations, not for-sale sites): the Town Centre Area Plan (OCP s. 10.4) update expanded the plan boundaries to incorporate River Bend, consolidated the land use designations, and added a Town Centre Core designation supporting higher densities in a transit-oriented downtown anchored by the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station; Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 covers the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station TOAs inside the plan area. These are policy designations over largely built parcels — any assembly is a private negotiation over built lots, not a listed vacant-land offering.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around East Central

items.t: The City publishes no boundary for the MLS "East Central" sub-area; the Town Centre Area Plan covers the downtown core at the west side of the sub-area, and its boundaries were expanded in the plan update to incorporate River Bend; the wider sub-area takes in the residential streets east and north of downtown toward 232 Street and 124 Avenue.

Schools physically inside the sub-area: Golden Ears Elementary (K–7), 23124 118 Avenue; Harry Hooge Elementary (K–7), 12280 230 Street; Thomas Haney Secondary (7–12), 23000 116 Avenue; ci:tməxw Environmental Community (K–8), 23125 116 Avenue; District 42 Alternative Secondary (9–12), 23125 116 Avenue. Catchments are address-based in SD42, which has no middle tier (elementary K–7, secondary 8–12).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in East Central

items.t: Lougheed Transit Corridor — adopted Jan 27, 2026: Official Community Plan Amending Bylaw No. 7781-2021 was given third reading and adopted at the Jan 27, 2026 council meeting (public hearing Jan 20, 2026; City news release Feb 4, 2026); the corridor runs from the City's western boundary to the Town Centre at 221 Street along Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road. Cite it as adopted.

Albion Area Plan: adopted Oct 28, 2025 as part of the City's fall 2025 OCP/area-plan update series (Town Centre, Hammond, Silver Valley and Albion) — Albion is east of this sub-area, but the same update series is the planning context for East Central's Town Centre changes.

SSMUH / suites / subdivision potential as the City states it: one secondary suite per lot inside the single detached building, maximum 40% of gross floor area, not within the floodplain area; eligible single-family and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws. Subdivision of an RS-1 lot must still meet the s. 605 minimums (668.0 m² / 18.0 m / 27.0 m) — SSMUH unit counts do not create new fee-simple lots by themselves.

Bare-land strata rules (where a bare-land strata lot is bought — the BC strata block applies in full to the lot): Form B diligence (fees, amounts owed, levies, CRF balance, insurance summary; provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions (younger spouse/partner, caregivers, legacy residents, defined children); a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no ALR ground was identified here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Central

items.t: East Central's land story is density policy, not vacant lots (2026): the Town Centre Core designation, the two Transit-Oriented Areas (Haney Place Exchange and Port Haney Station, Bylaw No. 8001-2024), the adopted Lougheed Transit Corridor (Bylaw No. 7781-2021, adopted Jan 27, 2026) and the Albion Area Plan adoption (Oct 28, 2025) in the same fall 2025 update series all push value into assemblies and added units on built lots — a buyer pricing a teardown on today's single-house use alone misses the documented policy direction, and a buyer pricing it as if rezoning were assured overpays for a designation, not an approval.

Civic cluster on the land a buyer is actually walking: Maple Ridge Leisure Centre, 11925 Haney Place; Memorial Peace Park on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road (City Hall, the ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall around it, with the Cenotaph, the Bandstand and the Haney Farmers Market); Maple Ridge Public Library, 130–22470 Dewdney Trunk Road, the only FVRL branch in Maple Ridge; Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre inside Haney Place Mall, 121–11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
Hospital: Ridge Meadows Hospital, 11666 Laity Street, is the community hospital for Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows with 24/7 emergency care, west of this sub-area.

Heritage at the southwest corner: Port Haney was historically the steamboat landing and CPR station for the area, and the Bandstand in Memorial Peace Park was presented by the Maple Ridge Concert Band as a gift to the people of Maple Ridge — the oldest land in this sub-area carries heritage context a teardown buyer should check before assuming a clean rebuild.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers in East Central

items.t: Zoning: Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019: Houses sit under RS-1 (Single Detached Residential), s. 605 — minimum lot area 668.0 m², minimum lot width 18.0 m, minimum lot depth 27.0 m, maximum lot coverage 40%; Town Centre parcels carry Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under the same bylaw.

Floodplain and escarpment: the south edge (River Road / Port Haney) sits along the Fraser River — the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), a covenant on title identifies construction in the floodplain, no habitable floor space may be located below the flood construction level on affected lots, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties. The Fraser River Escarpment policy area reaches the sub-area's west edge (its east boundary is 224 Street); lots within 300 m of the escarpment crest require a geotechnical report attached to a Section 219 covenant before a building permit. Which lots are affected is per-parcel.

blocks.text: East Central: streets and boundaries

items.t: East Central sits east of West Central and the Town Centre seam at 222–224 Street, west of Cottonwood, with Southwest Maple Ridge (Port Haney) at its southwest corner and Albion further east along Lougheed Highway; residents and the City usually call its west end Downtown Maple Ridge, Haney, or the Town Centre.

blocks.text: East Central: the housing stock

items.t: This sub-area holds two stocks side by side: freehold single-detached houses on the residential streets east and north of downtown, and strata condos concentrated in the Town Centre core along 224 Street, 226 Street, 227 Street and 121 Avenue.

The condo cluster exists because the plan allows it: the Town Centre Core designation supports higher densities in a transit-oriented downtown anchored by the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station.
The City names a downtown location "Brickwater" at 11897 227 Street.

blocks.text: East Central: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Town Centre Area Plan update expanded the plan boundaries to incorporate River Bend, consolidated the land use designations, and added a Town Centre Core designation supporting higher densities around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station.

Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 covers the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station transit-oriented areas inside this plan area, which changes the parking and density rules a downtown buyer or builder meets.
Town Centre parcels carry Town Centre commercial, multi-family and comprehensive development zones under Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019, separate from the house zones on the residential streets.

blocks.text: East Central: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Memorial Peace Park, on 224 Street between Lougheed Highway and Dewdney Trunk Road, is surrounded by City Hall, the Leisure Centre, the Greg Moore Youth Centre, The ACT Arts Centre and Haney Place Mall, holds the Cenotaph and the Bandstand, and hosts the Haney Farmers Market — downtown condos face event and market activity, not just retail.
The Maple Ridge Leisure Centre at 11925 Haney Place, at the west edge of this sub-area, has an indoor pool, fitness centre, gymnasium and sport courts.
Maple Ridge Public Library (Fraser Valley Regional Library) at 130 – 22470 Dewdney Trunk Road is inside this sub-area and is the only Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Maple Ridge.

The Ridge Meadows Urgent and Primary Care Centre is inside Haney Place Mall at 121 – 11900 Haney Place, open 7 days a week, 9:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; Ridge Meadows Hospital itself is west of this sub-area at 11666 Laity Street.
Port Haney, at the sub-area's southwest corner, was historically the steamboat landing and Canadian Pacific Railway station for the area.
